posts.title: Permanent Partner Visa: Your Two-Year Wait Plan
posts.excerpt: The 2-year wait for your permanent partner visa is a chance to prepare. Learn when you can apply and what to collect each month.
posts.content:
Quick Answer: A permanent partner visa is the second stage of the Australian partner visa. It is subclass 801 if you applied from inside Australia and subclass 100 if you applied from outside. Most couples become eligible two years after they lodge the combined application. It is not automatic, because you must prove your relationship is still genuine and continuing.

You lodged your partner visa. Now the long wait begins. Most couples ask the same question: what should we do with all this time?

This guide answers it. First, you will learn what the permanent partner visa is, when you can apply and how long it takes. Then you get a simple plan for what to collect, and when.

The plan works for both the 801 and the 100. Follow it and the permanent stage will feel calm instead of rushed.

Not sure which option fits you?

Book a consultation with a MARA-registered agent at SuccessVisa.

Book a Consultation

What is a permanent partner visa?

A permanent partner visa lets the spouse or de facto partner of an Australian citizen, permanent resident or eligible New Zealand citizen live in Australia for good. It is the final step of the two-stage partner visa process.

You apply for both stages at the same time. You pay one government fee. However, Home Affairs decides each stage separately.

Is a partner visa 820 a permanent resident visa?

No. The 820 is the temporary first stage. It lets you live, work and study in Australia while Home Affairs assesses your case. You become a permanent resident only when the permanent visa is granted.

Partner visa 801 vs 100: which one is yours?

Both visas give the same rights. The only difference is where you applied. Your permanent visa follows your temporary visa, so you do not choose it.

If you applied

Temporary visa

Permanent visa

From inside Australia

Subclass 820

Subclass 801

From outside Australia

Subclass 309

Subclass 100

This guide uses "permanent partner visa" for both. Where a point only applies to one, we say so.

Want to see how the full process works from day one? Read our [partner visa guide]([partner visa landing page link]).

When can you apply for the permanent partner visa?

In most cases, you become eligible two years after the date you lodged the combined application. The clock starts at lodgement. It does not start when your temporary visa is granted.

For example, say you lodged on 1 November 2024. Your usual eligibility date would be 1 November 2026. A late grant of the temporary visa does not push that date back.

Can you get the permanent partner visa sooner?

Sometimes. You may not need to wait the full two years if your relationship was already long when you lodged. As a general guide, that means:

  • you had been together for three years, or
  • you had been together for two years and had a dependent child with your partner.

These rules have detail and exceptions. Check your own dates with a registered migration agent before you plan around them.

Do you get the permanent partner visa automatically?

No. Reaching the two-year mark only makes you eligible for assessment. Home Affairs looks at your relationship again before it grants permanent residency.

For this reason, a break-up, weak evidence or old documents can still lead to a refusal at this stage.

Do you have to wait for an invitation?

Usually you do not need to wait to be chased. Many agents advise sending your updated evidence close to the two-year mark. Home Affairs may also contact you through your ImmiAccount. Check it often.

Not sure of your exact eligibility date? [Talk to our team]([contact page link]) and we will work it out with you.

Permanent partner visa timeline: what to do and when

The wait is long, but it is also your chance to build strong proof. Use this plan from the day you lodge. Dates below count from your lodgement date.

Months 0 to 3: set up your system

First, make one safe folder for everything, on paper and online. Next, save a copy of your lodged application and all the evidence you sent.

Then watch your ImmiAccount. Keep your address, passport and contact details up to date. Tell Home Affairs about any change.

Months 3 to 12: build a steady paper trail

At this stage, you simply live your life together and keep the records. Do not wait until the last month.

  • Keep joint bank statements and shared bills.
  • Save your lease or mortgage papers with both names.
  • Keep post addressed to both of you at one address.
  • Take dated photos at events, trips and family gatherings.

Months 12 to 18: add proof of your shared future

Now your evidence should show that the relationship has grown. Save travel records, holiday bookings and joint plans. Keep messages and emails from any time you are apart.

Also check your list of friends and family. You will need two people who know you both well. They must be 18 or over, and Australian citizens or permanent residents, to complete Form 888.

Months 18 to 22: refresh the hard documents

By this point, you can start the slower tasks. Check that your passport is valid. Ask your sponsor to confirm they are still an Australian citizen, permanent resident or eligible New Zealand citizen.

In addition, you and your partner should each write a fresh personal statement. Cover how you share money, home life and plans. Be honest and specific.

The last 2 months before your eligibility date: get ready to submit

First, order a new Australian Federal Police check. Also get police certificates from any country where you lived for 12 months or more in the last 10 years since turning 16.

Next, ask your two witnesses to sign their Form 888 declarations. Then check whether you owe any debt to the Australian Government, and sort it out.

Finally, put your updated evidence in order. Many applicants send it close to the two-year mark.

After you submit: respond fast

Home Affairs may ask for more documents or a new medical check. Answer by the deadline in the request. Late replies are a common cause of delay.

If you want a second pair of eyes on your folder, [book a partner visa evidence review]([contact page link]) before you submit.

What evidence do you need for the permanent partner visa?

Home Affairs looks at the same four areas it checked at the first stage. It wants new proof that covers the time since you lodged. Do not just resend old papers.

Area

What it shows

Examples

Financial

You share money and bills

Joint bank statements, shared bills, joint loans or assets

Household

You live together and share chores

Lease or mortgage in both names, joint post, a written chore split

Social

Others see you as a couple

Photos, joint trips, shared invitations, two Form 888 declarations

Commitment

You plan a long life together

Personal statements, messages when apart, plans for the future, children's birth certificates

Strong evidence is recent, specific and consistent. It should match what you told Home Affairs the first time.

Permanent partner visa document checklist

Exact requirements vary by case. Most applicants need these items:

  • Updated relationship evidence from your temporary visa period
  • Two Form 888 statutory declarations
  • A new Australian Federal Police check, plus overseas police certificates if needed
  • Passport photo page, and birth and marriage certificates
  • Sponsor details and proof of their citizenship or residency
  • A health examination, if Home Affairs asks for one
  • Proof you have repaid, or arranged to repay, any debt to the Australian Government

If children are on your case, check the rules for adding them. A child who does not hold your temporary visa may first need a Dependent Child visa (subclass 445) and Form 1002. This must happen before the permanent decision.

Need help sorting your documents? [See how our partner visa team can help]([partner visa landing page link]).

What if your life changes during the wait?

Life does not pause for a visa. Here is how common changes can affect you.

If you move house: Update your address in your ImmiAccount. Keep proof of the new shared address.

If you have a baby: Tell Home Affairs. Keep the birth certificate. A child you share can also strengthen your evidence.

If your passport changes: Update the new details through your ImmiAccount.

If you want to travel: Once you hold the temporary visa, you can usually travel. On a bridging visa, check your travel rights first, because leaving can stop you coming back. Also plan carefully around your eligibility date, because you may need to be in Australia when the permanent visa is decided.

If your relationship ends: Get advice straight away. In some cases you may still qualify for the permanent visa. These include:

  • your sponsor was violent to you or to a dependent child (family violence),
  • your sponsor has died and you can show your relationship would have continued, or
  • you share custody of, or have access to, a dependent child with your sponsor.

These cases are complex, and each one is judged on its own facts. If this is you, speak to our team in confidence as early as you can.

How long does the permanent partner visa take?

The permanent stage is usually much faster than the first stage. Home Affairs counts the time from your eligibility date, which is normally two years after you lodged.

Home Affairs shares times as two numbers. One shows how long it took to finish 50% of recent cases. The other shows 90%. In September 2026, published figures for the 801 were roughly 5 months and 12 months.

These are not promises. Missing documents, extra checks and complex cases can all make it longer. Always check the live Home Affairs processing times guide for the latest figures.

Home Affairs also asks people not to chase for updates while their case is within the normal range. Use your ImmiAccount instead.

How much does the permanent partner visa cost?

There is no extra government fee for the permanent stage. It was paid when you lodged the combined application.

From 1 July 2026, the combined partner visa charge is A$11,710 for the main applicant. Extra applicants add to this. You may still pay for new police checks, medicals, translations or agent fees.

What are the new partner visa rules for Australia in 2026?

Two changes matter most for people on the 820/801 path.

  • Higher fee. The charge rose to A$11,710 on 1 July 2026. This affects new applications, not the permanent stage of an existing one.
  • Priority order. Since 25 July 2026, Home Affairs processes under Ministerial Direction 117. Onshore partner visas (820 and 801) get the highest priority.

In the sources we reviewed in November 2026, we found no change to the two-stage system or to the two-year rule. Rules move quickly, so confirm the current position before you rely on this.

Want to know how a rule change affects your case? [Contact our team]([contact page link]).

Common permanent partner visa mistakes to avoid

Most problems are simple and avoidable. Watch out for these:

  • Sending old evidence that does not cover the last two years
  • Leaving gaps, such as months with no joint records
  • Giving details that do not match your first application
  • Missing a deadline in a Home Affairs request
  • Adding a child too late, or in the wrong way
  • Letting your witnesses' details or your sponsor's status go out of date

A small error can mean delays or even a refusal. For that reason, many couples have their file checked before they submit.

What do you get with a permanent partner visa?

Once granted, you become a permanent resident from that day. You can:

  • live, work and study in Australia without time limits,
  • enrol in Medicare,
  • join free English classes through the Adult Migrant English Program, if eligible,
  • sponsor eligible family members, and
  • travel in and out of Australia for five years from the grant date.

After five years, you need a Resident Return visa to keep returning as a permanent resident. You can check your travel dates on VEVO.

Can you become an Australian citizen after the permanent partner visa?

Yes, if you meet the rules. In general, you need at least four years of lawful residence in Australia. The last 12 months must be as a permanent resident. You must also meet the character requirement and pass the citizenship test.

Time spent outside Australia is limited, so check your own dates with the Department's residence calculator.

Permanent Partner Visa FAQs

Is a partner visa 820 a permanent resident visa?

No. The 820 is temporary. You become a permanent resident when the 801 is granted.

How long does it take to get a permanent partner visa?

You usually wait two years from lodging to become eligible. After that, recent published times for the 801 have been roughly 5 to 12 months. Check the live Home Affairs guide.

What are the new partner visa rules for Australia in 2026?

The fee rose to A$11,710 on 1 July 2026. Since 25 July 2026, onshore partner visas get top priority under Ministerial Direction 117. We found no change to the two-year rule.

Do I get the permanent partner visa automatically after two years?

No. You become eligible for assessment, and Home Affairs checks your relationship again.

Do I need to pay again for the permanent stage?

No government fee is due again. You may pay for police checks, medicals or agent help.

Can I get the permanent partner visa in less than two years?

Sometimes. A three-year relationship, or two years with a child, at the time you lodged may help.

What happens if we break up before the permanent visa is granted?

You may still qualify in limited cases, such as family violence. Get advice quickly.

Do I need an invitation to submit my documents?

Not usually. Many couples send updated evidence near the two-year mark. Check your ImmiAccount for any request.

Is the partner visa 801 the same as the 100?

They give the same rights. The 801 follows the 820 (applied inside Australia). The 100 follows the 309 (applied outside).

Can I work and study while I wait?

Yes, once you hold the temporary visa. On a bridging visa, your work rights depend on the visa you hold.

Can I include my child in the permanent stage?

Yes, in many cases. A child may need a Dependent Child visa (subclass 445) and Form 1002 before the decision.

Do I need a migration agent or lawyer?

No, but many couples use one to check their evidence. Only a registered migration agent or lawyer can give you visa advice.

Plan your permanent partner visa with confidence

The two-year wait is not dead time. Use it to build clear, honest proof of your life together. Then the permanent partner visa stage becomes a simple step, not a scramble.

To recap, save records from day one, keep your ImmiAccount current, and refresh your hard documents in the last few months. Above all, reply to Home Affairs on time.

Ready for the next step?

Not sure which option fits you?

Book a consultation with a MARA-registered agent at SuccessVisa.

Book a Consultation

Disclaimer: This article is for general information only. It is not visa, migration or legal advice. Visa rules, fees and processing times change often, and every case is different. Only the Department of Home Affairs decides visa applications, and no outcome can be guaranteed. Speak to a registered migration agent or lawyer about your own situation before you act.

posts.content:
Quick Answer: Most published prices from Australian migration agents fall between about A$4,000 and A$7,000 for both stages of a partner visa. Some charge less and some charge more. This is on top of the government fee, which is A$11,710 for the main applicant since 1 July 2026. Medicals, police checks and translations cost extra.

You know the partner visa is expensive. Now you want to know what an agent adds on top. That is a fair question, and the answers online are hard to compare.

This guide gives you real numbers and a clear way to judge a quote. First, you will see what agents charge. Then you will learn what is included, what costs extra, and when an agent is worth it.

The fees here are indicative figures from Australian agents' published pages in November 2026. Always get a written quote for your own case.

Not sure which option fits you?

Book a consultation with a MARA-registered agent at SuccessVisa.

Book a Consultation

How Much Do Migration Agents Charge for a Partner Visa?

Migration agent fees for a partner visa in Australia vary a lot. Published prices we reviewed ranged from about A$2,600 to A$8,000 for both stages. Most sat between A$4,000 and A$7,000.

Typical Partner Visa Agent Fees

What you are paying for

Typical published range

Notes

Both stages together (820/801 or 309/100)

A$4,000 to A$7,000

Most common range. Budget agents start near A$2,600. Some go up to A$8,000

Stage 1, the temporary visa (820, 309 or 300)

A$1,800 to A$3,900

Often the larger share of the work

Stage 2, the permanent visa (801 or 100)

A$800 to A$2,750

Check if it is included or priced separately

First consultation (about 45 minutes)

Free to A$160

Some agents credit it to your fee

Some agents show fees without GST. In Australia, GST adds 10%. Always ask whether a price includes it.

Why Do Agent Fees Vary So Much?

Two agents can quote very different prices for the same visa. These are the usual reasons:

  • Scope: One quote may cover both stages. Another may cover stage 1 only.
  • Case complexity: A short relationship, past visa refusals or a complex visa history take more work.
  • Number of applicants: Adding children or other family members can raise the fee.
  • Experience: Senior agents and lawyers often charge more.
  • Support level: Some quotes include replies to Home Affairs and interview help. Others do not.

A low price is not always a bad sign. However, check the scope before you say yes.

Not sure which range fits your case? [Talk to Our Team]([contact page link]) for a clear, written quote.

Government Fee vs Migration Agent Fees for a Partner Visa

The agent fee is not the visa fee. You pay two separate bills. The government charge goes to the Department of Home Affairs. The professional fee goes to your agent.

What Is the Government Partner Visa Fee in 2026?

The charge for the 820/801, 309/100 and 300 visas is the same. It covers both stages when you apply together.

Applicant

Charge from 1 July 2026

Main applicant

A$11,710

Additional applicant aged 18 or over

A$5,860

Additional applicant under 18

A$2,935

You do not pay a second government fee for the permanent stage. It was part of the first payment.

The visa charge is also non-refundable. You do not get it back if the visa is refused. For this reason, many people want a careful check before they lodge.

What Does the Full Partner Visa Cost with an Agent?

Here is a simple example for one applicant with no children. It uses a mid-range agent fee of A$5,500. This number is only an example.

Cost

Amount

Government visa charge

A$11,710

Agent fee (example)

A$5,500

Medical exam

A$350 to A$450

Total before police checks and translations

About A$17,600

Police certificates and translations are extra, and their cost depends on your countries and documents.

Want help working out your total? [See Our Partner Visa Services]([partner visa landing page link]).

What Do Partner Visa Migration Agent Fees Include?

A fair quote should say clearly what you get. Ask for it in writing.

What Is Usually Included in the Agent Fee

Most partner visa fees cover the core work:

  • A check of your eligibility and the best visa path
  • A document and evidence checklist
  • Help with forms and your relationship statement
  • Lodgement with the Department of Home Affairs
  • Replies to requests from the Department

What Is Often Unclear

Some items are included by one agent and charged by another. Ask about each one.

  • Stage 2: Is the permanent stage (801 or 100) in the same fee?
  • Interviews: Will the agent help if a case officer calls you?
  • Extra requests: Who pays for more work if Home Affairs asks for more proof?
  • Refusal: Is a review at the Administrative Review Tribunal (ART) included?

What Costs Extra

These costs are almost never part of the agent fee:

Extra cost

Typical amount

Medical exam

A$350 to A$450 per person

Police certificates

Varies by country

Document translations

Varies by document

Bridging visa B (to travel while you wait)

A$575 from 1 July 2026

ART review, if refused

A$3,727 from 1 July 2026

In addition, extra applicants add to the government charge.

You can read what to expect after lodging in our [permanent partner visa guide]([permanent partner visa article link]).

Fixed Fee, Staged Payments or Hourly: How Agents Bill

The way an agent charges matters as much as the price. It decides how much you can plan for.

Fixed Fee

The agent quotes one price for a set scope. This is the most common model for a partner visa. It is easy to budget, so ask what the price covers.

Staged Payments

You pay in parts. For example, one part when you start and one when the agent lodges. Staged payments also protect you if your plans change.

Hourly Rates

You pay for each hour the agent works. This can be fair for a small task. However, it can grow without a limit. If an agent bills hourly, ask for an estimate and a cap.

"No Visa, No Fee" Offers

Some firms offer to charge a reduced fee, or none, if the visa is refused. Terms differ and often have conditions. Read the fine print and ask what is refunded.

What About Full Payment Upfront?

Be careful if an agent wants the full amount before agreeing the scope. Ask for a written fee agreement first.

An agent cannot promise a visa outcome. Only the Department of Home Affairs decides.

Is It Worth Paying Migration Agent Fees for a Partner Visa?

It depends on your case. You do not need an agent to apply. However, the government fee is high and it is not refunded. A small mistake can be costly.

Can You Apply for a Partner Visa Without an Agent?

Yes. Many couples lodge on their own through ImmiAccount. This can work well if your case is simple and you have clear, well-organised proof.

It also means you carry the risk. You must understand the rules, build the evidence and reply to Home Affairs on time.

When an Agent Can Help the Most

An agent is worth a close look if any of these apply:

  • Your relationship is short, or you have not lived together for long
  • You have had a visa refused or cancelled
  • You are on a bridging visa, or your visa is about to end
  • You have children, or a complex family situation
  • You have a past character or health issue
  • You are short of time and want the paperwork done right

What an Agent Cannot Do

An agent can organise your case and explain the rules. They cannot guarantee a result. Be wary of anyone who does.

Only a registered migration agent or a lawyer can give you paid visa advice in Australia.

Thinking about getting help? [Book a Free Consultation]([contact page link]) and we will tell you honestly whether your case needs an agent.

How to Compare Partner Visa Migration Agent Fees and Avoid Red Flags

A lower price is not always a better deal. A higher price is not always better service. Use the steps below to compare quotes fairly.

Step 1: Check the Agent Is Registered

Search for the agent on the official register of the Office of the Migration Agents Registration Authority (OMARA). Look for their MARN, which is their registration number. Lawyers are checked through their state law society.

Step 2: Ask for a Written, Itemised Quote

The quote should show the agent fee, GST, and the government charge as separate lines. It should also list which stages and tasks are included.

Step 3: Ask These Questions

  1. Does the fee cover both stages, or only stage 1?
  2. What happens if Home Affairs asks for more evidence?
  3. Is a review after a refusal included?
  4. How and when do I pay?
  5. What is refunded if I change my mind or the visa is refused?

Red Flags to Watch For

  • No price or price range anywhere, and no written fee agreement
  • Open-ended hourly billing with no estimate or cap
  • Full payment demanded before the scope is agreed
  • A promise or guarantee that your visa will be granted
  • A quote far below others, with a very narrow scope
  • Pressure to sign on the spot

If you see two or more of these, pause and get a second opinion.

Want a clear, itemised quote with no surprises? [Contact Our Team]([contact page link]).

Did the Partner Visa Fee Increase in 2026?

Yes. The partner visa application charge rose by about 25% on 1 July 2026. The change applies to the 820/801, 309/100 and 300 visas.

Fee

Before 1 July 2026

From 1 July 2026

Main applicant

A$9,365

A$11,710

Additional applicant, 18 or over

A$4,685

A$5,860

Additional applicant, under 18

A$2,345

A$2,935

Bridging visa B

A$190

A$575

ART review fee

A$3,580

A$3,727

The agent fee is set by each agent. It did not rise by a fixed amount. Some agents may update their prices, so ask for a current quote.

Will the Partner Visa Fee Go Up Again?

Home Affairs usually adjusts its charges on 1 July each year. We cannot tell you the next amount. Check the official fee page before you lodge.

If you are planning to apply, an early start helps you budget. [Speak with Our Team]([contact page link]) about timing and costs.

Migration Agent Fees for Partner Visa Australia: FAQs

How Much Is the Fee for a Partner Visa?

The government charge is A$11,710 for the main applicant since 1 July 2026. An agent adds a professional fee, often A$4,000 to A$7,000 for both stages. Medicals, police checks and translations are extra.

Will the Partner Visa Fee Increase in 2026?

It already did. The charge rose about 25% on 1 July 2026, from A$9,365 to A$11,710. Home Affairs usually adjusts charges each 1 July, so check before you lodge.

Is It Better to Use a Migration Agent for Australia?

It can be, especially for complex cases such as a short relationship, a past refusal or a bridging visa. Simple cases can be lodged without an agent. No agent can guarantee a result.

How Much Do Immigration Consultants Charge in Australia?

Fees depend on the visa. For a partner visa, published prices run from about A$2,600 to A$8,000 for both stages. A first consultation is free or costs up to about A$160.

Is the Agent Fee Separate from the Government Fee?

Yes. You pay the agent for their work. You pay the government charge to the Department of Home Affairs. A good quote shows both clearly.

Do I Pay Again for the Permanent Stage?

You do not pay a second government fee. Some agents charge separately for stage 2, so ask whether it is in your quote.

Can I Pay a Migration Agent in Instalments?

Often yes. Many agents use staged payments, such as part at the start and part at lodgement. Agree the schedule in writing.

Are Cheap Migration Agents Safe?

A low price can be fine, but check the scope. Confirm the agent is registered, ask what is included and be wary of any guarantee.

Do I Get My Agent Fee Back if My Visa Is Refused?

It depends on the agent's written terms. The government visa charge is not refunded after a refusal.

Is the First Consultation Free?

Some agents offer a free first consultation. Others charge about A$99 to A$160 for 45 minutes and may credit it to your fee.

Can I Negotiate Migration Agent Fees?

You can ask. However, a lower price often means a narrower scope. Compare what is included before you compare the price.

Do I Need a Migration Agent to Apply for a Partner Visa?

No, it is not required. Many couples apply on their own. An agent can help if your case is complex or you want the paperwork checked.

In Short

Migration agent fees for a partner visa in Australia usually run about A$4,000 to A$7,000 for both stages. The government charge is separate: A$11,710 for the main applicant since 1 July 2026. Medicals, police checks and translations cost extra.

Compare the full cost, not only the price. Ask what each quote includes, get it in writing, check the agent's registration and be wary of any promise of a result. A good agent will explain every cost before you commit.
